fact_text: P/E equals the share price divided by earnings per share, where EPS is net profit over a period divided by the total number of shares outstanding.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Master Price to Earnings Ratio in 14 Minutes and Value Stocks Like a Pro! | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-30)

fact_text: The analyst warned that P/E alone does not show whether a stock is undervalued or overvalued and should be read alongside other ratios and company analysis.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Master Price to Earnings Ratio in 14 Minutes and Value Stocks Like a Pro! | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-30)

fact_text: A company that declares a loss in a period has no P/E ratio, so the ratio shows as not available rather than as a number.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Master Price to Earnings Ratio in 14 Minutes and Value Stocks Like a Pro! | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-30)

fact_text: P/E is usually calculated on trailing annual EPS, while an expected P/E uses the research team's forecast for quarters not yet reported.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Master Price to Earnings Ratio in 14 Minutes and Value Stocks Like a Pro! | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-30)

fact_text: The analyst's screen compares a company's P/E with its sector average, so multiples above the sector average look expensive and multiples below it look cheap.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Master Price to Earnings Ratio in 14 Minutes and Value Stocks Like a Pro! | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-30)

fact_text: On 30 Nov 2024 the average P/E of the banking sector was about 4.22 times, based on trailing annual EPS.
